candidates.title: Turn a monthly review deck into a video outline

demandEvidence.chore: Prepare a business review deck as a short narrated video for a team, investors, or clients.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: if you send your team, your investors or your clients a review deck every month

experimentPlan.output: A concise narration outline for one operator supplied monthly review deck, with each statement linked to a supplied slide or figure.
inputs: A fictional or operator supplied review deck with non-sensitive figures
A chosen audience such as team, investors, or clients
A short list of approved company and brand terms
experimentPlan.trigger: The operator supplies a deck and selects the intended audience for a monthly review.
steps: Read the supplied deck and identify its headings and figures.
Draft a short narration outline in the selected audience tone.
Attach each factual sentence to a slide heading or figure.
Flag unsupported statements or missing context for review.
Return the outline for a person to correct and approve.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: On a fictional deck, verify every numeric statement matches its cited slide and every unsupported conclusion is flagged rather than added.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies a sanitized deck, confirms its figures and audience, and approves all narration; this experiment does not render or send a video.
unverified: Reliable extraction from varied slide layouts
Whether the monthly task occurs across enough independent buyers
Any paid demand for an AI narration service

ease.reason: A student can draft a short narration from an operator supplied sample deck, but no attached source documents a separate implementation tool.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: consultants or small firms preparing monthly review decks may pay for narration help; the post establishes no buying intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week test can turn a supplied fictional deck into a checked script; the source describes a video workflow, while the proposed script avoids unverified rendering.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable draft is possible, but a person must supply the deck, check figures and approve narration; no unattended execution is established.

evidence.reason: The fresh post gives a monthly deck-to-video use case and setup notes in retained spans, but not repeated customer evidence or independently validated demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a narrow script draft is testable, but no implementation reference or buyer corroboration is attached and the post does not establish demand beyond its use case.

candidates.title: Keep received product images with reply context

demandEvidence.chore: Use an already received customer image and message together when preparing a product inquiry for reply review.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Customers can send either text messages or images.

experimentPlan.output: A review card pairing a customer message with its received image and a proposed catalog match for a human reply reviewer.
inputs: A synthetic image or image description
A small operator supplied product catalog with labels
experimentPlan.trigger: A test message record includes text and an image already available to the operator.
steps: Keep the supplied text and image in one test record.
Compare the image with the small supplied catalog.
Draft a tentative product label and explain the match.
Flag uncertain or unmatched cases for manual review.
Return a reply suggestion only after the reviewer checks the match.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Use labeled synthetic examples and confirm the correct catalog match is suggested or uncertainty is flagged; no message is sent automatically.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies permitted test records, verifies any product match and approves replies; live Messenger access and image handling are outside this proposal.
unverified: Make route configuration that carries image and text together
Image interpretation accuracy on real customer photos
Permission and privacy controls for live customer media

ease.reason: A student can test paired fictional message and image records, but no attached reference supports image interpretation or Make routing.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small service businesses answering product inquiries may pay to reduce repeated image requests; the post proves no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mock can pair supplied test images with text and flag an item from a supplied catalog; Messenger access and product matching are unverified.

autonomy.reason: A draft can be assembled repeatedly, but a person must verify the image match and approve every reply; no integration execution is documented.

evidence.reason: The retained post describes a concrete image handoff issue and desired shared agent context, but provides no frequency or corroborating demand.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: the post contains a clear handoff chore, but the proposed useful matching capability and integration lack attached implementation support.

candidates.title: Map form answers into a review sheet

demandEvidence.chore: Transfer Google Forms answers into Google Sheets for review.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Connecting Google Forms to Google Sheets

experimentPlan.output: A proposed spreadsheet row mapped from one supplied form response, with missing or ambiguous fields flagged.
inputs: A fictional form response with agreed field labels
A mapping sheet approved by an operator
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies a sample form response and the target review columns.
steps: Map each field to an operator-approved column.
Flag missing or ambiguous values without guessing.
Produce a row preview with source field labels.
Ask a person to verify before any spreadsheet entry.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: For labeled synthetic responses, compare each preview cell with its declared source field and ensure missing values remain flagged.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The operator supplies sample records and field mapping, reviews each row, and performs any live entry; no Forms or Sheets connection is tested.
unverified: Whether this offer reflects a repeated customer chore
Correct mappings for real forms and changing schemas
Any live Make, Forms, or Sheets execution

ease.reason: A student can map fictional form answers to a table, but the supplied source does not document the named integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: small professional service operators may pay to reduce form transfer work; this service offer establishes no buyer intent or payment.

feasibility.reason: A four-week mapping mock is bounded, while actual field mapping, Make execution and persistence are unsupported by the supplied source.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable row draft is possible, but a person must review entries and handle exceptions; no automation execution is evidenced.

evidence.reason: The post advertises Forms-to-Sheets connection help and practice work, but does not describe a specific customer case or recurring need.

candidates.reason: Below threshold: a specific integration is offered as a service, but the post does not identify a customer request or recurring case and no implementation reference is supplied.

steps.message: Assessed all ten assigned discussion posts. Three concrete task ideas received five-criterion proposed experiments but remain below the unrounded threshold; seven posts lack a concrete bounded chore or request in supplied spans. No post proposed.
